chunk_text: Vector search latency after index rebuild Severity: medium. Systems: atlas-search, pgvector-store. Services: retrieval-api. Symptoms: p95 search latency exceeded 4 seconds; retrieval requests queued behind index maintenance. Root cause: HNSW index rebuild completed while planner statistics were stale and rebuild jobs were allowed to run concurrently. Resolution: Refreshed planner statistics, reduced concurrent rebuild jobs, and added a post-maintenance latency check. Synthetic incident narrative: Atlas Search saw slow vector retrieval after a scheduled index rebuild. The problem was not an embedding model issue. The root cause was stale planner statistics combined with concurrent index maintenance. The resolution refreshed statistics and limited rebuild concurrency.

Worker queue stalled after malformed webhook payload Severity: high. Systems: harbor-events, queue-worker. Services: webhook-ingest. Symptoms: queue depth increased for 37 minutes; new webhook jobs stopped completing. Root cause: A malformed but accepted webhook payload triggered a retry loop without dead-letter routing. Resolution: Added schema validation, moved failing jobs to a dead-letter queue, and replayed valid events. Synthetic incident narrative: Harbor Events stopped processing incoming webhook jobs even though the worker process stayed alive. The durable queue kept growing because a malformed payload was repeatedly retried. The fix added stricter validation and dead-letter handling before replaying safe jobs.

Dashboard showed stale metrics after cache promotion Severity: medium. Systems: northstar-ui, metrics-cache. Services: dashboard-api. Symptoms: dashboard panels did not update; API returned older metric windows. Root cause: A cache promotion changed the key prefix but the invalidation job still targeted the previous prefix. Resolution: Updated invalidation keys, flushed affected cache entries, and added a prefix consistency test. Synthetic incident narrative: Northstar dashboards displayed old data after a cache promotion. API health checks passed because cached responses were valid but stale. The root cause was a cache key prefix mismatch between writers and invalidation. The fix aligned prefixes and flushed affected entries.

Batch caption exporter produced duplicate rows Severity: low. Systems: media-foundry, caption-pipeline. Services: metadata-exporter. Symptoms: JSONL export contained repeated asset IDs; downstream training job rejected the batch. Root cause: Pagination retry logic appended a completed page twice after a transient timeout. Resolution: Added idempotent page tokens, deduplicated by asset ID, and generated a corrected export. Synthetic incident narrative: Media Foundry exported duplicate caption rows into a JSONL batch. The issue was limited to export assembly, not caption generation. A transient timeout caused one page of results to be appended twice. The fix added idempotent pagination and asset-level deduplication.

Agent memory write path accepted missing provenance Severity: high. Systems: memory-hub, agent-runtime. Services: memory-write-api. Symptoms: new memories had empty source fields; retrieval audit could not explain some answers. Root cause: A client-side form marked provenance as optional while the server accepted null source metadata. Resolution: Made provenance required server-side, rejected incomplete writes, and backfilled affected synthetic records. Synthetic incident narrative: Memory Hub accepted writes without source provenance, making some agent answers harder to audit. The root cause was a mismatch between client form requirements and server validation. The fix enforced provenance at the API boundary and backfilled affected synthetic entries.

Tokenizer upgrade changed evaluation scores Severity: medium. Systems: eval-lab, benchmark-runner. Services: scoring-worker. Symptoms: regression dashboard dropped without model changes; token counts increased for long prompts. Root cause: A tokenizer dependency upgraded implicitly because the benchmark environment lacked a lockfile. Resolution: Pinned tokenizer versions, regenerated baseline scores, and added dependency fingerprinting to reports. Synthetic incident narrative: Eval Lab reported lower scores after a dependency refresh even though the evaluated model was unchanged. Investigation found an implicit tokenizer upgrade that changed prompt segmentation. The resolution pinned dependencies and added environment fingerprints to future benchmark reports.

Search API returned empty results for restricted memories Severity: medium. Systems: atlas-search, policy-gateway. Services: retrieval-api. Symptoms: authorized restricted-memory searches returned zero hits; public-memory searches still worked. Root cause: A policy filter compared tenant visibility labels case-sensitively after a schema migration. Resolution: Normalized visibility labels, repaired migrated rows, and added mixed-case policy tests. Synthetic incident narrative: Atlas Search returned no restricted-memory results for authorized callers, while public searches continued to work. The issue was not vector recall. A schema migration introduced mixed-case visibility labels and a case-sensitive policy check. The fix normalized labels and added policy tests.

File watcher missed rapid config rotations Severity: low. Systems: config-bridge, runtime-loader. Services: config-sync. Symptoms: service used old config until restart; watcher logs showed one event for two rotations. Root cause: The watcher coalesced rapid file events and did not verify final file checksums. Resolution: Added checksum polling after watcher events and slowed automated rotations to one active update at a time. Synthetic incident narrative: Config Bridge failed to load the newest runtime configuration when two rotations happened close together. The file watcher observed one event but skipped the second final state. The fix added checksum confirmation after each event and serialized automated rotations.

Embedding batch job exhausted temporary disk Severity: high. Systems: embedding-farm, object-staging. Services: embedding-batch. Symptoms: batch job crashed at 82 percent; temporary staging volume reached 100 percent. Root cause: Intermediate shard files were retained after successful upload instead of being removed per batch. Resolution: Deleted completed shards, added disk budget checks, and streamed future uploads without local retention. Synthetic incident narrative: Embedding Farm failed near the end of a batch run because temporary shard files filled the staging volume. Uploaded shards were retained locally instead of being deleted. The fix cleaned completed shards, added disk budget checks, and changed future uploads to stream mode.

Alert router paged the wrong service owner Severity: medium. Systems: signal-router, ownership-map. Services: alerting. Symptoms: page went to retired owner group; current owner saw the alert late. Root cause: Ownership metadata was updated in the catalog but the alert router used a stale exported map. Resolution: Regenerated the exported map, added daily freshness checks, and showed owner source timestamps in alerts. Synthetic incident narrative: Signal Router sent an alert to a retired owner group because its exported ownership map was stale. The service catalog had the correct owner, but the alert router did not refresh its copy. The resolution regenerated the map and added freshness checks.

Model download mirror served partial artifact Severity: high. Systems: model-mirror, artifact-cache. Services: model-download. Symptoms: clients failed checksum validation; download retries returned the same partial file. Root cause: The mirror promoted an incomplete artifact after a network timeout because checksum verification ran after promotion. Resolution: Moved checksum verification before promotion, quarantined partial artifacts, and invalidated mirror cache entries. Synthetic incident narrative: Model Mirror served a partial artifact that failed client checksum validation. Retry attempts returned the same bad file because the mirror had promoted it to cache. The fix required checksum verification before promotion and quarantine of incomplete artifacts.

Runbook search ranked glossary pages above fixes Severity: low. Systems: runbook-index, ops-search. Services: documentation-search. Symptoms: search results surfaced definitions before fix procedures; operators clicked through multiple irrelevant pages. Root cause: The ranking profile over-weighted exact term matches and ignored document type boosts. Resolution: Boosted procedure documents, lowered glossary weight, and added query tests for fix-oriented searches. Synthetic incident narrative: Ops Search ranked glossary pages ahead of actionable runbooks for fix-oriented queries. Exact keyword matches overwhelmed document type signals. The fix boosted procedure documents, lowered glossary weight, and added tests for queries that ask how to resolve incidents.
